"The Longer the Base, The Higher in Space"

The longer the base, the higher in space" is a classic Wall Street stock market adage meaning that an extended period of price consolidation leads to a larger and stronger price move when a breakout finally occurs. A long base structure serves several purposes. It shakes out and frustrates weak shareholders, builds energy, and, when it breaks out, removes overhead selling supply. Gold is a fantastic example of this phenomenon. In late 2024, gold broke out of a massive, 14-year base. The Gold ETF (GLD) would double in less than two years.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: TradingView

After consolidating in a long, frustrating base through the summer, the Nasdaq 100 Index ETF (QQQ) is threatening to break out of a more than three-month-long base structure. If QQQ can break and hold above the June 3rd, 2026 highs ($748.65), the Fibonacci extension suggests traders can look for an $800 target on QQQ.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: TradingView

Mid-Term Election Cycle Seasonality Flips Bullish

Thus far in 2026, the market has been closely following historical mid-term election cycle seasonality trends. Historically, stocks rally in the first quarter, then consolidate in the summer as money managers take vacations, and investors reduce risk ahead of election uncertainty. However, investors who have preserved capital through the summer may be in for a treat. According to Ryan Detrick (@RyanDetrick) of Carson Investment Research, "October has been the best month in midterm years historically and November the second best." Since 1950, the S&P 500 Index has delivered returns in each month ~70% of the time, with October's average gain 3% and November's average gain 2.7%.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Carson Investment Research

Oil: False Breakout

Soaring energy prices have acted as the proverbial "pebble in the shoe" for equity markets. Earlier this month, the United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) broke out of a three-month base. However, the breakout quickly failed, with USO falling in five consecutive sessions.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

An old Wall Street adage suggests that "From false moves come fast moves." Meanwhile, on Tuesday, a deep-pocketed trader began selling call options in USO. Call selling can be a stronger tell for investors than put buying because it indicates that smart money is willing to take on more risk. This week, the President of Iran is in New York for the first time since the start of the war. Is a deal imminent?

Micron Earnings Loom

Micron (MU) has been one of the leading artificial intelligence names of the current cycle. The AI hardware provider will report earnings next week that could act as a catalyst for the tech sector. Although MU stock is off its recent highs, its earnings track record has been spotless lately, with the company beating Zacks Consensus Analyst Estimates in 13 consecutive quarters.

title: AI Skeptics Surrender Again as Traders Eye Path Forward for Tech
detail:
AI Skeptics Surrender Again as Traders Eye Path Forward for Tech
Bloomberg · Bloomberg
Jessica Menton
Wed, September 23, 2026 at 6:27 AM MDT 4 min read
^NDX

(Bloomberg) -- The road to the Nasdaq 100 Index's first record since June was anything but straightforward. Now the equity bulls that helped drive the move are looking for evidence that momentum won't peter out.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Nvidia's Stock Is Flashing a Warning Sign as Valuation Drops

Apple Developing New Fitness Tracker Aimed at Rivaling Whoop

Trump Hails Iran Talks Even as Tehran Sets 'Firm Positions'

Dangote Hires Engineers India for $16 Billion Kenya Refinery

Meta's Muse Drags Down Stocks That Depend on 'Consumer Inertia'

They've added $22 billion into technology-focused US exchange-traded funds this quarter, compared with $4.6 billion into the rest of the market, data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence show. And more recently, hedge funds boosted their net-long Nasdaq 100 futures positions to the highest level since December, according to the latest data from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

While the advance in the tech-heavy gauge has been stellar and earnings robust, uncertainty around tensions in the Middle East, persistent inflation and the Federal Reserve's efforts to tame it still linger. And with so much riding on the AI trade, the setup suggests little room for error.

"Investors still feel optimistic about AI given that corporate earnings are really strong," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis, whose firm is overweight cyber security, software and chip stocks and underweight sectors including consumer staples and real estate. "But we need to continue to see upward earnings estimate revisions for the biggest tech companies for the rally to continue."

The Nasdaq 100 gained 0.8% on Tuesday, closing at a record high and reversing a brutal stretch earlier this year that pushed the gauge down more than 10% from its peak. The S&P 500 Index closed little changed on and is within 0.5% from reclaiming its record in August.

And Wall Street is positioning for the rally to continue. US stocks saw the largest net buying in five weeks last week, with software firms leading the charge, according to Goldman Sachs Prime Services. US equity funds attracted nearly $64 billion in weekly flows through Sept. 16, the most in three months, according to Bank of America strategists citing EPFR Global data. Cash, meanwhile, had the largest outflow in nine weeks.

"The AI rally still has more room to run and we don't see investors pulling back on risk anytime soon," Athanasios Psarofagis, an ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said by phone. "The flows into tech stocks isn't anywhere near extreme yet to be a contrarian indicator to dump those stocks. It's very hard to derail this momentum. The show goes on."

U.S. stock futures moved slightly higher on Wednesday as investors monitored developments around Meta Platforms' (NASDAQ:META) Muse AI agent, Middle East diplomacy and upcoming U.S. business activity data.

At 02:57 ET, Dow futures were up 41 points, or 0.1%, while S&P 500 futures gained 7 points, or 0.1%. Nasdaq 100 futures also rose 0.1%, adding 27 points.

The major Wall Street indices recorded mixed performances in the previous session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined, the S&P 500 was unchanged and the Nasdaq Composite advanced.

Analysts at Vital Knowledge described Tuesday's trading as "fairly quiet," with investors also following developments surrounding the conflict with Iran and their potential implications for energy prices, inflation and interest rates.

Meta's Muse Draws Investor Attention

Artificial intelligence remains another focus following the launch of Meta's Muse AI agent earlier in September.

Initial adoption of the app has coincided with gains in semiconductor stocks, while shares of some financial services and travel companies have declined amid investor assessments of how AI agents could affect their businesses.

Muse has partnered with companies including PayPal and financial technology platform Plaid for services involving areas such as payments and financial planning.

The S&P 500 financial services sector fell 2% in the previous session. JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Raymond James and Ameriprise Financial were among the stocks that declined, while Charles Schwab and LPL Financial each fell more than 6%.

Travel-related stocks also came under pressure as investors considered the potential use of AI agents for planning and booking trips.

Zuckerberg Due to Speak at Meta Event

Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg is scheduled to speak at a company event on Wednesday, with Muse and Meta's broader AI strategy expected to be among the areas followed by investors.

Meta shares have risen more than 20% since Muse was released on September 8, adding more than $200 billion to the company's market capitalisation over the period.

Attention is also likely to remain on the industry's approach to AI safety and the level of investment required to develop the technology.

Meta and other large technology companies have announced substantial spending plans for AI infrastructure, including data centres and semiconductors.

Brent Crude Remains Below $100

Brent crude remained below $100 a barrel on Wednesday as markets followed diplomatic developments involving the U.S. and Iran and changes in Middle East oil supply.
